messages:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up — I opened a short proposal for attribute coalescing heuristics + a tiny ingest shim that can dedupe/compact redundant trace attributes at the gateway before we envelope. link: https://rfd/internal/obs/attr-coalesce (TL;DR below)

jon: skimming. is the idea to mutate the envelope on the fly?

maya: Not mutate app payloads. The shim would rewrite our internal envelope only at the edge ingest (short-lived), coalescing repeated keys across spans in the same bundle and emitting a compact representation that downstream can expand if needed.

sam: Hmm. Primary win is smaller envelopes and lower egress/storage, right? Any accuracy tradeoffs for billing attribution?

maya: Exactly — lower bytes and less indexing. Tradeoffs: 1) late enrichment becomes trickier (we'd need deterministic rehydrate rules), 2) some query shapes that relied on per-span duplicate attributes may need translation. I sketched a stability contract in the RFC.

liz: Could you paste a tiny example of before/after?

maya: Sure — example (pseudo):

```json
{"spans": [
  {"id": "s1", "attrs": {"svc": "payments", "region": "us-east1", "user_id": "u1"}},
  {"id": "s2", "attrs": {"svc": "payments", "region": "us-east1", "user_id": "u1"}},
  {"id": "s3", "attrs": {"svc": "payments", "region": "us-east1", "user_id": "u2"}}
]}
```

becomes compacted to:

```json
{ "coalesced": {"svc": "payments", "region": "us-east1"},
  "per_span": [ {"id":"s1","attrs":{"user_id":"u1"}}, {"id":"s2","attrs":{"user_id":"u1"}}, {"id":"s3","attrs":{"user_id":"u2"}} ]
}
```

maya: The idea is that common keys with identical values across a bundle are pulled up into a coalesced map. Downstream systems either expand or they query using the coalesced map + per_span overrides.

jon: That seems fine for common keys like svc/region. But what about keys with high cardinality (user_id) — we should never coalesce those. How do we choose?

maya: My proposal: ruleset with three buckets — always-coalesce (static low-cardinality keys we own), never-coalesce (high-cardinality or PII), and adaptive heuristics (coalesce if >N spans in bundle share same value and global-cardinality < threshold). Defaults in RFC: always = [svc, region, env], never = [user_id, request_id, email], adaptive threshold = 3 spans / global-cardinality < 1000 per minute for that key.

sam: Concern: billing key resolution. We currently resolve billing via the first-seen billing_key attribute during sampling. If coalescing changes where that lives, we need invariant: billing_key lookup semantics must be identical for every pipeline.

maya: Agreed. Contract: shim must materialize a synthetic per-span billing_key when we know coalesced value applies. We add a normalization pass that ensures billing_key is present in per_span attrs for any downstream system that expects it. That keeps attribution unchanged.

liz: Nice. How do we validate correctness?

jon: We should run parallel canary ingest where we keep both raw and coalesced envelopes, compute a diff metric: billing_mismatch_rate, query_result_delta, ingest_bytes_saved, index_write_changes. If billing_mismatch_rate > 0.1% -> rollback.

eng-bot: deploy: canary pipeline created for ingest-shim/attr-coalesce. CI job: ingest-canary-runner.

maya: Proposed rollout plan in RFC: prototype in staging -> collect diffs for 48h -> canary in us-east for 7d (10% traffic) -> increment if diffs negligible and bytes savings > 5%.

sam: What about cross-bundle queries that assumed repeated attributes for simple indexing? Eg, queries that do `WHERE svc = 'payments' AND user_id = 'u1'` — if svc is coalesced, index builders must see it.

maya: Good point. Two options: 1) index builder expands coalesced map at write-time (preferred), 2) keep a small forward index referencing coalesced values. I lean 1) to preserve query surface.

jon: Index-time expansion will cost CPU but keeps query engine unchanged. I like that. Also add a telemetry tag `ingest.coalesced_v1=true/false` on spans so we can trace back anomalies.

liz: Edge-case: mixed-value detection in a single bundle where most spans share a value but one differs. If we coalesce, we must include per_span overrides to avoid silently misattributing. Make sure schema expresses overrides clearly.

maya: Yup — per_span override wins. Coalesced acts as default. We'll include strict validation in the shim and a debug-mode that logs discrepancies for the first 10k bundles.

sam: Who owns the RFC follow-up work?

maya: Volunteer list in RFC: jon -> prototype shim, sam -> validation harness + billing parity tests, liz -> index-write expansion POC, maya -> rollout plan + metrics.

jon: I'll start a branch and drop a tiny shim binary in `ingest/edge/shims/attr_coalesce` with flags: `--mode=sample|rewrite|noop` and `--rules-file`. Will stub rules first.

maya: Perf target: add < 2ms median to edge path and reduce stored bytes by >6% on avg for high-churn services. If median >5ms then fallback.

liz: Add a feature flag so we can turn coalescing off per-service during canary.

eng-bot: action_added: jon assigned to prototype, sam assigned to billing parity harness, liz assigned to index expansion POC, maya added as reviewer. due: 2026-04-01

sam: one more thought — sampling interaction. If bundles are sampled partially, we must ensure coalesced values reflect sampled subset semantics. Eg. if only 1 of 4 spans sampled, coalescing could hide the presence of svc on unsampled spans. We need explicit rules: coalesce only from sampled+unsampled combined view at ingest, not from sampled subset.

maya: Good catch. We'll derive coalesced values from the full bundle at ingress (before sampling is applied) so sampled query semantics stay consistent.

jon: ok starting branch. I'll push a WIP README with examples and the `--rules-file` format.

maya: Thanks all. Quick TODOs: jon prototype, sam harness, liz index POC, maya finalize policy doc. We'll sync next Wed. :thumbsup:

jon: ack.
